record.paper_title: Whitehead's Asphericity Question and Its Relation to Other Open Problems
record.original_question: For presentations of groups with weight 1 and deficiency 1, can the asphericity argument based on an injective block in the Fox-Jacobian matrix be extended beyond the semidirect-product case to other such groups?

evidence.quote: Can we extend this argument to other groups of deficiency and weight 1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a group given by a finite presentation $\langle x_1,\dots,x_n \mid r_1,\dots,r_mangle$ of deficiency one (i.e., $n-m=1$) and weight one (i.e., the normal closure of some single element of the free group on $x_1,\dots,x_n$ has the same normal closure as $\{r_1,\dots,r_m\}$ after adding one generator, equivalently $G$ has weight one as a normally generated group). Let $J =  ig(\partial r_i/\partial x_j ig)\in M_{m	imes n}(\mathbb{Z}G)$ be the Fox–Jacobian matrix of the presentation, where $\partial/\partial x_j$ denotes the Fox free derivative followed by the projection $\mathbb{Z}F	o\mathbb{Z}G$.

For presentations $G$ that are semidirect products $Ntimes\mathbb{Z}$, asphericity of the standard 2-complex of the presentation can be established by exhibiting an $m	imes m$ block of $J$ that, viewed as a $\mathbb{Z}G$-linear endomorphism of $(\mathbb{Z}G)^m$, is injective (equivalently, the corresponding submatrix is a non–zero-divisor in $M_m(\mathbb{Z}G)$); injectivity of this block forces the second homotopy module of the presentation 2-complex to vanish.

Problem: Determine whether this injective-block criterion can be extended to all (or a strictly larger class of) finitely presented groups of deficiency one and weight one beyond those that are semidirect products with $\mathbb{Z}$. Concretely: does every aspherical finite presentation with $n-m=1$ and weight one admit some $m	imes m$ submatrix of its Fox–Jacobian matrix $J$ that induces an injective $\mathbb{Z}G$-module map $(\mathbb{Z}G)^m	o(\mathbb{Z}G)^m$, and if not, identify the maximal subclass of weight-one deficiency-one presentations for which such an injective block exists and certifies asphericity?
artifact.status_search_result: The Whitehead asphericity question remains unresolved, and the broader study of asphericity for deficiency-one, weight-one presentations is an active area. No source located indicates that the Fox–Jacobian injective-block method has been extended beyond the semidirect-product case to a general class of such presentations; the problem appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: A new approach to Whitehead's asphericity question
status_evidence.snippet: The Whitehead asphericity question is still unanswered, although some interesting advances have been obtained.

status_evidence.claim: Asphericity criteria for deficiency-one presentations remain a topic of ongoing research.
